launch-ny-new-york-city-prospect-park.description: Long Meadow is the park's broad north-side lawn; the Picnic House and nearby restrooms make this a practical gathering zone, but event setup and wet turf can affect access.
The lake and historic Boathouse sit in the park's southeast half. Use Ocean Avenue or Lincoln Road approaches and expect a substantial walk from Grand Army Plaza.
Children's Corner groups the carousel, Lefferts Historic House, and nearby family attractions near Flatbush Avenue; each attraction keeps its own schedule and fees.
Prospect Park Zoo is a separately ticketed attraction near the Flatbush Avenue side, not a free park amenity; use the zoo entrance rather than navigating to the park center.
LeFrak Center at Lakeside hosts seasonal skating, roller activities, water play, rentals, and food. Hours, admission, and activity availability change by season.
The Nethermead is a large central meadow reached by internal paths; Dog Beach is elsewhere near Long Meadow and has specific dog-use rules rather than all-day off-leash access.

launch-ny-new-york-city-flushing-meadows.description: The Unisphere is the clearest central landmark. Arrive via Mets-Willets Point and follow the World's Fair promenades; fountain operation is seasonal and not guaranteed.
The Queens Museum and New York State Pavilion occupy the World's Fair core. The museum is ticketed by suggested admission and the pavilion is generally viewed from outside.
Playground for All Children is an accessible family destination on the Corona side with a nearby comfort station; it is far from the tennis-center transit entrance.
Meadow Lake and its boathouse are in the park's southern half. The lake loop is long, exposed, and separated from central attractions by highways and internal roads.
Queens Zoo is a separately ticketed attraction on the west side of the central park. Check zoo hours and entry requirements rather than relying on park hours.
The USTA tennis center is a separate venue beside the 7 train. US Open security, tickets, and event circulation can change access throughout the surrounding park.

launch-ny-new-york-city-the-high-line.description: The Gansevoort entrance is the southern terminus near the Whitney Museum and provides elevator access. It is often one of the busiest entry points.
Chelsea Market Passage around West 15th and 16th Streets has seasonal food, seating, restrooms, and an elevator connection near a very busy cross-section of the route.
The 10th Avenue Square uses stepped seating and a large street-facing window. It is a rest stop and overlook, not an exit to the avenue below.
The West 23rd Street section includes lawn and seating areas; elevator access can change with maintenance, so verify status before relying on it.
The northern High Line enters Hudson Yards, loops through the Rail Yards, and reaches the Spur near West 30th Street with ramp and elevator access points.

launch-ny-new-york-city-brooklyn-bridge-.description: Pier 1 combines lawns, promenade, ferry access, restrooms, and broad harbor views. Use 1 Water Street for Access-A-Ride and expect heavy weekend crowds.
Empire Fulton Ferry includes Jane's Carousel, lawns, food nearby, and classic bridge views. Carousel admission and hours are separate from park entry.
Main Street and Pebble Beach sit between the Manhattan and Brooklyn bridges. The beach is for sitting and viewing; entering the river is unsafe and prohibited.
Pier 2 has courts, skating and recreation with seasonal hours, lockers, and a comfort station. Activities and concessions may have separate fees.
Pier 5 offers sports fields, a boathouse, picnic tables, and designated grills. Tables and grills are first-come unless a permit or event restriction applies.
Pier 6 contains multiple playground zones and the seasonal Water Lab. Playgrounds close at sunset and water operation is weather-dependent.

launch-ny-new-york-city-hudson-river-par.description: Pier 25 is a major Tribeca family and recreation pier with playgrounds, sports, mini golf, food, restrooms, and river views; operators keep separate schedules.
Pier 40 is the park's large sports and operations hub. Its courtyard, fields, parking, and restrooms have distinct entrances and hours.
Gansevoort Peninsula has lawns, sports, river access, a beach-like shoreline, dog run, and restrooms. Posted water-contact rules still apply.
Little Island is a separately managed free public park reached by bridges from Hudson River Park. Capacity controls, events, and its 9 PM closing differ from the surrounding park.
Pier 57's public rooftop offers free views and seating, with indoor food and restrooms below. The rooftop generally closes earlier than Hudson River Park.
Chelsea Waterside Park is an inland family and recreation area with a playground, sports, dog run, and seasonal facilities near West 23rd Street.
Pier 97 is the northern recreation pier with playground and gathering spaces. It closes earlier than the overall park and can be affected by events or weather.

launch-ny-new-york-city-the-battery.description: Battery Playscape is a large flood-resilient playground with five ecology zones. It is free and generally open 7 AM-6 PM, shorter than the surrounding park.
SeaGlass Carousel uses illuminated fish vehicles rather than traditional horses. Tickets cost $6 and seasonal, weather-dependent hours should be checked before arrival.
Castle Clinton is a free National Park Service site and the landmark beside Statue Cruises ticketing and security. Building hours are shorter than park hours.
The perennial gardens and Battery Oval provide the park's quieter landscape. Stay on paths and check lawn conditions after rain or during event setup.
Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island ferries use the Castle Clinton area. Only the authorized ferry operator serves the islands; tickets and airport-style screening take extra time.

launch-ny-new-york-city-bryant-park.description: The central lawn is open when turf and event conditions allow. A closed lawn does not mean the surrounding promenades, chairs, food, or activities are closed.
Le Carrousel is a small paid carousel on the 40th Street side near a public restroom. It keeps seasonal hours separate from the park.
The outdoor Reading Room provides free books, newspapers, and programs without requiring a library card; hours and programming are seasonal.
Free board games, chess, ping pong, and activity zones sit around the lawn. Equipment hours and availability depend on staffing and events.
Winter Village replaces the lawn with a seasonal market and skating rink. Rink admission may be free with a reservation, but skate rental and premium times can cost extra.

launch-ny-new-york-city-governors-island.description: The Hills include Outlook, Discovery, Grassy, and Slide Hill. Slide Hill has long slides and climbing routes; the entire South Island zone closes at dusk.
Hammock Grove has suspended hammocks and play lawns in the South Island landscape. Hammocks are first-come and the zone closes at dusk.
Liggett Terrace is a central food, seating, fountain, and event area. Weekend restrooms and vendor hours can differ from general island hours.
Picnic Point is at the island's southwest tip with skyline and Statue of Liberty views. It is a long walk from Soissons Landing and closes at dusk.
Nolan Park is the historic green surrounded by former officers' houses, often used for arts and cultural programming. Individual buildings may not be accessible.
Soissons Landing is the main arrival from Manhattan with visitor information and an accessible restroom in Building 110. Confirm the return ferry schedule before exploring.

launch-ny-new-york-city-riverside-park.description: Pier I at West 70th Street anchors Riverside Park South with river views, seating, a seasonal café, restroom, lawns, and nearby playgrounds.
Hippo Playground at West 91st Street has swings, slides, sand, spray shower, shade, picnic seating, drinking fountain, and a public restroom.
The West 96th Street red clay courts require NYC Parks tennis permits or single-play tickets during the season. A portable restroom is nearby.
The 91st Street Garden is a volunteer-tended flower garden and quiet destination. It is separate from Hippo Playground despite sharing a cross street.
Dinosaur Playground near West 97th Street has play equipment, water play, and a restroom. Playground hours are shorter than park hours.
Ellington in the Park and the West 105th Street fields provide food, restrooms, and recreation on the lower level; use a cross-street route that reaches the correct elevation.
